newsitem.title: USA: Fergie says royal family wanted to punish her.
newsitem.headline: Fergie says royal family wanted to punish her.

text.p: Britain's disgraced Duchess of York said the royal family was so incensed after her separation from Prince Andrew that they wanted "me to move into a house with the bathrooom outside."

In an interview with ABC's Diane Sawyer to be shown on Wednesday night on "PrimeTime Live," the red-haired duchess, popularly known as Fergie after her maiden name Sarah Ferguson, said she would move to the United States "like a shot" if she could take her two children with her.

She said she gets along very well with her ex-husband but she would never want to rejoin the royal family. "I am very content and we get along very well. But I think it is better to be free. I think the system's too much for me. The system. The firm, the gray men, the institution, it chokes me."

Asked how she was treated by Andrew's family after her separation, the duchess said, "They wanted me to move into a house with the bathroom outside. These are the queen's grandchildren." She was referring to a bid by the royal family to have her move to a smaller house.
She said she never fit into the family. "I wasn't right. I wasn't from royal stock. And then, of course, I hung myself with my rope because they gave me a lot of rope and I hung myself."

The duchess denied a report that she once had been placed on a suicide watch, saying, "No, that's not true. It's not the sort of word I've ever contemplated. I have two wonderful children and ... I'm on my way to inner peace, I think."

The interview signals the start of a media blitz to promote her autobiography in which she describes the events that led to her 1992 separation from Andrew, which included her being photographed topless in the south of France while her toes were kissed by her financial adviser, Texan John Bryan. She and Prince Andrew were divorced six months ago.
The duchess said she fortified herself with brandy and valium when she had to go tell Queen Elizabeth about the photographs the day before they were published.
"She was very disappointed in me, I think. Because you are talking about her beloved son, you know. It's very difficult." She added that she was sure that she let the queen and the royal family down.

On her current relationship with Andrew, she said, "He still does believe in me. I can't be all that bad, can I really? If he's still there by my side. And the papers can't be all that right either, can they?

"If he's still there by my side, (that) says a lot for him. But I'm there for him, too. Let's not forget that. I think it's not a one-way street. It's only because all my life has been on the front pages, but what about everyone else's life? We're both equal, both play the same tune and we both dance the same dance. And it takes two to tango."

She admitted to having "an overspending disease" and said, "A lot of people have done a lot worse. You could be an alcoholic or you could be an addict of some sort." She called it her form of bulemia, a reference to the eating disorder Princess Diana, the ex-wife of Prince Charles, suffers from.

Fergie's efforts to solve her financial woes with a perfume deal with cosmetics giant Revlon fell through, company spokeswoman Nancy Risdon said on Sunday. The duchess had hoped to make $10 million to wipe out her highly publicised debts, the Sunday People newspaper reported, but Risdon said the plan never got off the ground.
